footer: Compiled from Reuters, AP, PAHO, WHO, CNN, TechCrunch and Horizon reports filed on 18 November 2026 (full day, WIB).
sources_note: All seven stories were reported on 18 November 2026 (full day, WIB); the Gulf escalation, Peltola win, measles status and Ebola milestone were verified across multiple outlets.

stories.headline: Iran hits US bases in Bahrain and Kuwait; US strikes back
stories.summary: Iran's Guards sent drones at a US radar in Bahrain and Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait; allies say they were intercepted. US jets then hit a missile site on Qeshm Island.

stories.headline: Ukraine strike partly collapses Crimean Bridge
stories.summary: Kyiv struck the bridge linking Russia to Crimea for a second straight day, bringing part of the road span down into the strait below.

stories.headline: Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat in Democratic flip
stories.summary: Mary Peltola defeated incumbent Dan Sullivan in the last undecided Senate race, giving Democrats a 56-44 majority, their largest since 2009. She is the first Alaska Native senator.

stories.headline: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years
stories.summary: PAHO ended the status held since 2000 after 5,412 cases in 2026, the most since 1991, and 10 deaths. Mexico and Bolivia lost the status too.

stories.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases
stories.summary: WHO kept its global emergency in place as cases doubled in three months to over 11,000, with about 5,400 deaths, the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever.

stories.headline: Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen as APEC opens
stories.summary: China's Xi promised tariff cuts and wider market access at the APEC CEO summit, while Trump held Quad talks in Manila and announced a trade deal with the Philippines.

stories.headline: Nvidia revenue doubles to $115.8bn post-Huang
stories.summary: The chipmaker beat forecasts with revenue up 103% year on year and guided to $130bn next quarter, but its board said ousted CEO Jensen Huang will not return.

subtitle: Seven stories that defined Wednesday, 18 November 2026
title: THE WORLD TODAY
